note: GROK'S EMPTY CELL IS NOT A FINDING. grok's domains.service array is empty as an absence of MATERIAL, not as evidence that grok has no service plane. grok's own moduleCoverage records three service-domain modules that were read but never written up as mechanisms: xai-grok-workspace-daemon ('Service-domain process plumbing' - double-fork + setsid, single-instance pidfile lock, preview-proxy supervision, daemon-owned files opened O_NOFOLLOW mode 0600), xai-acp-lib ('The ACP transport itself: agent/client channel pair, gateway sender/receiver, message boxing, line-buffered and stdin readers, normalization ... belongs to service'), and xai-grok-http ('Infrastructure underneath the service and ops domains; contributes no mechanism of its own' - four shared reqwest clients). hintCorrections additionally remaps xai-grok-tools-api and xai-grok-voice INTO service. grok's service plane therefore demonstrably exists; it just carries no verbatim mechanism names in the inventory, so hard rule 1 forbids citing any of them in members. Read this domain's grok column as 'not inventoried', never as 'absent by design'. Note also that grok's domains.model and domains.ops are empty under the same deferral, and that the two domains.service items in the harvest file are xai-grok-pager slash-command renderings (/scroll-debug, /settings), i.e. TUI command material rather than transport, so they are not mechanisms of this domain and are excluded from the counts.

unmergedDoubts.whyNotMerged: Both are 'one binary/process serving several service roles' and codex's modules list includes exec-server. I did not merge because the codex mechanism's four helper roles (apply-patch, linux sandbox, windows sandbox, filesystem helper) are confinement helpers owned by the safety domain, so the shared content is only the argv[0] multiplexing trick; and grok's daemon has no verbatim name in domains.service, so hard rule 1 already forbids citing it. The grok half is carried as a member-less row instead.

I merged dsh's HTTP carrier into the HTTP service host row because in dsh the webserver route registry IS the registration seam for the /api bridge. One consequence is recorded here: IH's single web-service mechanism describes BOTH its unary HTTP route surface and its one WebSocket mux, and rule 2 lets it appear once, so I placed it in the HTTP row and added an ihNote to the WebSocket mux row and the trust-fence row instead of citing it three times. IH's mux does carry live session streams (chunk/reasoning/agent-state), which is why the WebSocket mux and SSE rows are close cousins of the HTTP row rather than cleanly disjoint.

Upstream splits the listener from the OpenAPI/SDK generator, while the fork bundles listener lifecycle, route-tree composition and lazy /doc into one mechanism and then adds a separate legacy-spec-compat mechanism. I therefore placed the fork's bundle in the listener row and the fork's legacy compat transform in the vendor/codegen row, so the fork's OpenAPI code sits in one row while its listener sits in the other. A reader must not read the fork's bundle as double-counted.

The descriptor generator and the Remote plane are two halves of one design and could be one row; I kept them separate because generation is build tooling with no Cordis plugin row while the plane is the runtime dispatch surface, and merging would also have pulled in the boot/profile seam that composes them, which is a third distinct capability.

All three push or receive server-side state outside the request/response cycle. Not merged because dsh's bridge is an in-tree browser consumer of a Host-event allowlist, codex's relay is an outbound dial to a vendor backend with enrollment, chunking and cursor resume, and dsh's webhook ingress is HMAC-verified inbound ingress from third-party systems: three different trust directions, not one capability.

Both propagate credentials into a live service session. Kept apart because dsh's is a redacted, revisioned, read-through RPC namespace (fail-closed, secrets never serialized) whereas cc-custom's is an unauthenticated stdin frame that mutates process.env directly (fail-open by design). The security posture is opposite, so a merge would hide the difference that matters.

codex's app-server mechanism de facto covers stdio bidirectional JSON-RPC control, so it arguably belongs in the bidirectional SDK stdio row. I kept it out because its distinguishing content is carrier multiplicity (stdio + private 0600 UDS + raw WS + Off, flock-serialised startup, stale-socket unlink) over one shared framed surface, which no other source has; the handshake and backpressure clauses are separate codex mechanisms so they cannot be folded into the same citation either.

The vendor/codegen row is built from codex's generated-contract export plus opencode's OpenAPI/SDK codegen and the fork's legacy spec transform. codex's headless JSONL exec surface names stdout JSONL among its flags, so it could have been routed to the one-way output row instead; I placed it with the export row because its differentiating capability is the --output-schema / --output-last-message machine contract rather than the line format, which is the same 'the published wire contract is a product' idea. cc-custom's output-format/exit-code mechanism stayed in its own row because it is a one-way consumer contract with no generated artifact.

IH's frozen v0 contract carries a session/history replay surface and cc-custom's replay/dedup is an acknowledged input stream over the same stdio channel, so a merge is arguable. Kept separate because IH's is read-side history the client drives explicitly (the server never replays to a fresh subscription) while cc-custom's is write-side idempotence (one uuid executed at most once, duplicates answered with isReplay:true).

Merged into one vendor/codegen row, but the lost detail is real: codex vendors TypeScript plus JSON Schema in two disjoint stable/experimental export sets with zstd-precomputed bundles, while opencode serves a lazily built OpenAPI document and compiles SDK clients behind a manifest. The merged label hides that codex's artifact is schema-for-SDK-authors while opencode's is a served HTTP document.

Merged into one workspace-routing/control-plane row, but the two are not the same maturity: upstream has a RequestPlan parser plus the /experimental/control-plane/move-session operation, while the fork has the full reverse proxy (HTTP and WebSocket) and the x-opencode-sync fence wait. A reader should not read the merged row as 'both do proxying'.

All four are one ACP server over stdio and are merged, which flattens two differences. (1) Maturity: upstream's adapter is initialize+prompt with runUntilIdle gating, the fork implements the full load/fork/list/resume/close lifecycle. (2) Permission philosophy: IH uses a binary autoApprove switch with no session/request_permission flow (a refused prompt never reaches the session service), dsh downgrades to one-shot allow-once/reject-once so a client response can never become a durable grant, and the opencode pair route prompts through the engine. That divergence is why the row is 已存在 rather than rewrite.

Service authentication is split into a launch-token/HMAC-cookie row (dsh) and a Basic-auth-plus-exemptions row (opencode pair, plus codex's capability-token / signed-bearer JWT upgrade gate). One row was arguable; kept apart because they differ in what they bind (an authority-bound signed cookie vs a long-lived static credential) and because codex's is an upgrade-time gate rather than a per-route middleware.

codex and cc-custom both expose the harness itself as an MCP server over stdio and are merged; cc-custom's control-channel bridge stayed separate because it carries MCP traffic in the opposite direction (servers the SDK consumer registered in-process, inside the SDK protocol). Merging would have conflated 'IH as MCP server' with 'MCP over the IH control channel'.

These are the five modules grok's own moduleCoverage/hintCorrections assign to service, including the ACP wire layer, which would otherwise be the strongest candidate for the ACP row. None may be cited in members because grok's domains.service array is empty and hard rule 1 requires verbatim presence in the inventory for this domain. Recorded here so the empty grok column is read as an inventory hole, not a design choice; the daemon module is given a member-less row so it is not dropped on the floor.

coverage.note: 56 = the sum of domains.service lengths across the seven sources (ih 5, dsh 15, codex 9, opencode-upstream 7, opencode-fork 8, cc-custom 12, grok 0). Each of the 56 appears in exactly one row; every source mechanism is cited at most once. Rows carrying an ihNote describe behaviour IH does have but whose mechanism is cited in another row (IH's web-service mechanism spans HTTP surface + mux + trust fence and can only be cited once).
